name: Urolithin A

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Worm lifespan and rodent muscle studies (2016)

track.title: Pilot in people
track.line: First-in-human safety trial in older adults (2019)

track.title: Dietary supplement

what.text: Urolithin A is made by gut bacteria from ellagitannins, plant compounds found in pomegranates, nuts and berries. Researchers describe it as a mitophagy inducer: it helps cells clear out worn mitochondria, the parts that make energy.
How much urolithin A a person makes from food varies with their gut bacteria. Most human trials of urolithin A taken directly were sponsored or funded by one company, Amazentis SA.

src.label: Singh et al., Cell Rep Med, 2022

what.text: Urolithin A is sold as a dietary supplement. FDA does not review supplements for safety or effectiveness before sale.

research.text: Urolithin A has been tested in several small randomized trials in people, lasting 4 weeks to 4 months. Most were funded by the company that makes it. Results on muscle were mixed: some endurance and strength measures improved, but most main outcomes did not. No trial has measured aging or lifespan in people.
Each is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Older adults' muscle endurance, 2022

facts.v: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, Seattle; sponsored by Amazentis
66 adults aged 65 to 90 (mean 72; 76% women; all White): 33 urolithin A, 33 placebo
4 months of 1,000 mg a day or placebo
6-minute walk and hand-muscle energy (ATP) production (main outcomes); muscle endurance; blood markers

research.found: The main outcomes did not differ from placebo. Hand and leg muscle endurance improved more at 2 months, and some blood markers, including C-reactive protein, fell. Adverse events did not differ.

src.label: Liu et al., JAMA Netw Open, 2022

research.title: Middle-aged adults' strength and fitness (ATLAS), 2022

facts.v: Randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled, two doses (500 mg and 1,000 mg), sites in Canada per the registry; sponsored by Amazentis, whose staff wrote the paper
Overweight middle-aged adults aged 40 to 65; 90 enrolled per the registry
4 months
Peak power output (main outcome), muscle strength, peak oxygen use, 6-minute walk, blood and muscle markers

research.found: Peak power, the main outcome, did not improve. The authors report about 12% more muscle strength and better fitness and walking scores, and lower blood acylcarnitines and C-reactive protein.

src.label: Singh et al., Cell Rep Med, 2022

research.title: Trained male distance runners, 2025

facts.v: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, during an altitude training camp; funded by Amazentis
42 competitive male runners (mean age 27): 22 urolithin A, 20 placebo
4 weeks of 1,000 mg a day
Fitness, running economy, 3,000 m time trial (in 22), muscle damage markers, muscle biopsies (in 20)

research.found: Running performance did not improve. Effort ratings and a muscle damage marker were lower after the time trial. Aerobic capacity rose within the group but did not differ significantly from placebo.

research.title: Immune cells in middle-aged adults, 2025

facts.v: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; funded by Amazentis, which supplied the product
50 healthy middle-aged adults (registry: ages 45 to 70)
4 weeks of 1,000 mg a day
Types and metabolism of blood immune cells; inflammation markers

research.found: Urolithin A raised a subset of less-exhausted CD8 T cells and their fat-burning capacity, and changed several other immune cell measures. These are lab markers, not illness or infection outcomes.

research.title: Blood vessel function in adults with obesity, 2026

facts.v: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, University of Oklahoma; authors reported no conflicts
50 adults aged 40 to 64 with BMI 30 or more (74% women): 25 per group; 7 lost to follow-up
4 weeks of 1,000 mg a day
Artery flow-mediated dilation (main outcome); other vessel tests; brain blood-flow responses

research.found: No improvement in artery function or other vessel tests. Brain blood-flow responses during a task were larger; task performance did not change.

src.label: Pinaffi-Langley et al., JAMA Netw Open, 2026

research.title: Safety in older adults, 2019

facts.v: Randomized, blinded single- and multiple-dose study (250 mg to 2,000 mg), France; sponsored by Amazentis
Healthy, sedentary older adults; the registry lists 60 enrolled, ages 61 to 85
Single dose, or 4 weeks of daily dosing
Safety (main outcome); blood levels; blood and muscle markers of mitochondria

research.found: The authors report a favorable safety profile. Doses of 500 mg and 1,000 mg for 4 weeks changed blood acylcarnitines and mitochondrial gene activity in muscle.

research.text: In worms (C. elegans), urolithin A extended lifespan. In two mouse models of age-related muscle decline, and in young rats, it improved exercise capacity. These results have not been shown to translate into longer life in people.

us.text: Urolithin A is not an FDA-approved drug. It is sold as a dietary supplement. FDA had no questions about one company's conclusion that it is safe for use in certain foods (GRAS notice 791, 2018). FDA does not review supplements for safety or effectiveness before sale. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: GRN 791, filed by Amazentis SA in June 2018, covers use in protein shakes, meal-replacement drinks, oatmeal, bars and yogurts. FDA closed it on December 20, 2018 with a 'no questions' letter. A search of FDA's GRAS inventory found no other urolithin notice.

side.text: In trials of up to 4 months, urolithin A was reported as well tolerated, with adverse events similar to placebo. Long-term safety in people has not been studied. FDA does not review supplements for safety before sale.

items.text: no statistical differences in adverse events between urolithin A and placebo (66 people).

unconfirmed: We could not open FDA's GRN 791 response letter PDF itself; the facts come from FDA's GRAS inventory record.
The ATLAS trial abstract does not give how many people took part; 90 enrolled per ClinicalTrials.gov.
We could not confirm urolithin A's status with Health Canada, the MHRA or UK Food Standards Agency, EU regulators (EFSA and EUR-Lex refused automated requests) or the TGA.
We found no record that urolithin A was filed with FDA as a new dietary ingredient; FDA's NDI list has no urolithin entry.
surprises: Urolithin A is often promoted for muscle, but in the two 4-month trials the main outcomes (walk distance, muscle energy production, peak power) did not improve; the gains were in secondary measures.
Almost every human trial we found was sponsored or funded by one company, Amazentis SA.
A 2024 test of urolithin A and NMN supplements found amounts as far as 100% below the label claim.
